# Dashboard Page

> Generated by the repository UI/UX Pro Max script (installed CLI version 2.2.3), then adapted to
> the current Angular page. The engine's generic dashboard queries did not reliably
> match a personal finance dashboard; current application structure and technical
> contracts take precedence.

Generator command:

```sh
python3 .github/prompts/ui-ux-pro-max/scripts/search.py 'Personal finance mobile dashboard: monthly spending overview, budgets, expense categories and installment commitments, Angular 16 Bootstrap 4 ng-bootstrap SCSS Lato warm brown existing design system' --design-system --format markdown --project-name Xpenses --persist --page dashboard --output-dir .github
```

## Page structure

- Start with the selected payment method and billing period, with clear previous/next
  controls and a human-readable date range.
- Surface period-level balance, income, expenses, and available variable spending before
  secondary analysis. Keep amount labels and period context adjacent.
- Present daily spending, expense composition, categories, and installment purchases as
  distinct sections with explanatory text where totals include estimates or scheduled
  charges.
- Keep the `Proyección y alertas` diagnosis and budget consumption visible without
  expanding anything. Use a clear section heading, the contextual status message,
  and a prominent percentage with its progress bar.
- Place the diagnosis after daily tracking and before the category overview so its
  message is visible before detailed expense analysis.
- Put income margin, daily variable spending, closing projection, and expense composition
  inside a native, initially closed `details` disclosure. Keep expansion reversible by
  keyboard and touch. Daily tracking remains before categories.
- Budget consumption means total period expenses divided by income; it is separate from
  variable-budget availability. Preserve the existing projection-alert and consumption-bar
  thresholds, which describe different signals. Composition retains two groups: variable
  expenses, and recurring expenses with installments.

## Responsive behavior

- Preserve the compact two-column KPI layout on phones and use the Bootstrap grid for
  wider layouts.
- Allow headings, period labels, and currency values to wrap without horizontal scroll.
- Keep period navigation, payment selection, date shortcuts, and expand/collapse controls
  reachable by keyboard and touch. Expose selected/expanded state and meaningful labels.
- Keep charts understandable with labels and amounts in addition to color; provide a
  reset path when category filtering changes the chart.

## Feedback states

- Keep loading skeletons in the space of the content they replace.
- Show a recoverable error with a retry action when dashboard data cannot load.
- Explain empty or estimated values in context. Distinguish estimates from recorded
  charges in both labels and totals.
- Without income, show a neutral message instead of a green zero-percent consumption
  or a favorable income margin. Keep actual percentages above 100% visible; cap only
  the visual progress fill and expose a valid numeric ARIA range with the actual
  percentage described in accessible text.
- Follow the shared brand tokens, Lato typography, and surface treatment in
  [the master design system](../MASTER.md) and [technical guide](../../../../docs/project-guidelines.md).
